raw_response:
I am getting old, so I do not chase trouble on 9 mu. Cotton is still what I know best, and on this small area I would rather manage it steadily than gamble on something new. I have high school education, so I do look at input rates and timing more carefully than before, but in the end I still trust what I have seen on my own land. If spring moisture is only average, I will prepare the field well, use a good hybrid cotton seed, put most of the fertilizer down early, then leave some nitrogen for later if the plants are growing strongly. Water from the well helps, but pumping costs money, so I will irrigate at the key stages instead of watering too often. I have only two people in the household, and cotton needs repeated attention, so I will keep the plan manageable and hire a little labor if picking becomes too concentrated. My goal is not the highest yield in the county, just a stable crop and decent income without overspending at the start.
